senses.gloss: ch. sameto take off, undress. Part. pass. חָלִיץ.
units: <cite ref="Targum Jonathan on II Samuel 6:20">Targ. II Sam. VI, 20</cite>.—Lam. R. introd (R. Joh. 1) <he>חֲלִיצֵי מסאני</he> without shoes.
<cite ref="Moed Katan 22b:6">M. Kat. 22ᵇ</cite> <he>למִיחֲלַץ</he> to bare their shoulders.
<cite ref="Yevamot 102b:14">Yeb. 102ᵇ</cite> <he>עמא דח׳ ליה … מיניה</he> a people from which its lord has withdrawn (with ref. to <he>חלץ מהם</he>, <cite ref="Hosea 5:6">Hos. V, 6</cite>).

senses.gloss: to perform the rite of ḥălitsah; v. infra.

to perform or arrange the rite of ḥălitsah. Ib. לה אחין וכ׳ (or דחלְצוּ) ואילו יבמה דחַלְּצוּ suppose brothers would untie the shoe of their sister-in-law, would this be of any legal consequence? Ib.ᵃ אנא לא הואי חַלִּיצְנָא וכ׳ I should not have allowed a ḥălitsah except &c.; a. fr.
